name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).

    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1457
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1457
- **Title**: ci(1267): path-triggered legs under dispatch-only CI (N1 AC1 + N2 lock-smoke) + nightly-red filer resurrection (N3)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1267-path-triggered-legs` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +597
- **Deletions**: -54
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T16:09:16Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T20:45:54Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1267 (slice 2 of the epic: N1/AC1 + N2/AC2 + N3/AC3; N4/AC5 remains, see Delivered vs remaining).

Motivating incidents, both CLOSED: #1265 (native build break arrived via an uncommitted lockfile — no PR surface at all) and #1266 (macOS app-suite regression whose only surface was nightly-only). AC4 linkage: both closed before this slice.

## Delivered

**N1/AC1 — path-triggered exclusion-zone leg under dispatch-only CI.** Slice 1 (#1350) landed `flutter-app-exzone` path-BLIND: it ran on EVERY SM validation dispatch because the `changes` classifier had no pull_request event to diff. This slice makes the classifier derive the validated diff itself: on `workflow_dispatch` it computes `merge-base(origin/main, HEAD)` (the PR fork point; the changes checkout is already fetch-depth: 0). A lib/src-only PR no longer pays for the macOS JS-engine leg; a `flutter_app/lib/apps/**` / `lib/src/js_ext/**` / exclusion-test diff does. Classification failure fails SAFE — the rare-path arms run unconditioned (over-triggering costs minutes; under-triggering hides a nightly-only red, the gh-1307/#1309 class). The four group outputs stay with the non-PR filter step, so main dispatches keep the full gate.

**N2/AC2 — lockfile-modified release smoke.** Lockfile committed + `--enforce-lockfile` everywhere already landed (gh-1296/gh-1265). Missing piece: the native linux/windows desktop targets were nightly-only, so a lockfile float (#1265's transitive `flutter_inappwebview`) had no pre-merge surface. New `flutter-app-lock-smoke` matrix (ubuntu + windows) runs `flutter build linux|windows --release` ONLY when the diff modifies `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` — same path-triggered model as exzone, same pinned SDK (`3.47.x`) and Linux toolchain as the nightly build-release legs. The resolve rides the shared `--enforce-lockfile` composite action (#726 retry + skew fail-fast), so a pubspec/lockfile skew fails loudly before any build. A red smoke reddens the required `Quality gate` (platform class per #1368: blocks the merge, never the pure-Dart publish). PRs not touching the lockfile pay nothing.

**N3/AC3 — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation.** Root cause of five silent red nights (last living tracker #466): the dedup lookup read jq's literal `"null"` (empty result of bare `.[0].number`) as a truthy issue number and died commenting issue `"null"` — never filing. Fixed with `.[0].number // empty` in BOTH steps (the shape ci.yml's ci-red-report already uses). Additionally:
- the job arms on `schedule` AND on a new `fileTracker=true` workflow_dispatch input — the AC3 synthetic-red drill (dispatch a forced-failing nightly with the flag → tracker filed/commented within the same run); manual dispatches without the flag stay tracker-silent;
- close-on-green stays schedule-only (a drill dispatch is not a night and must not close the live tracker);
- the decision — filed / commented / closed / why-not — is logged to the job output AND the step summary on every run (an empty decision log is how the filer stayed dead);
- two consecutive red SCHEDULED nights add `nightly-red-escalated` (streak = completed schedule-event failures before this run, current run excluded, dispatch runs never count; green resets naturally).

Note on #1364: that card is the `flake_watch.py` `--search`-based dedup (unquoted `(#<digits>` title fragment) — a DIFFERENT dedup in DIFFERENT code; untouched here, as scoped. The nightly filer's dedup is label-scoped JSON + jq, immune to the search-quoting class.

**Guards.** `test/ci_1267_path_triggered_legs_test.dart` + `test/nightly_filer_1267_test.dart` pin the wiring (structural lint over the workflow YAML — the repo's static-assert pattern, cf. `ci_binaries_arch_gate_test.dart`); `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart` AC3 count 12 → 13 for the new leg's action use (documented in place).

## Delivered vs remaining (issue ACs)

- AC1 ✅ (path-triggered on both events; a PR touching the external `packages/js_widget_runtime/` arrives as a `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin → exzone runs; lib/src-only → skips)
- AC2 ✅ (lock-smoke on lockfile diff; not touching → skipped)
- AC3 ✅ (filer resurrection + drill flag + decision log + escalation — verified by the drill dispatch once CI runs; remote-only surface)
- AC4 ✅ both incidents closed (linked above)
- AC5 / N4 ❌ remaining: merge-snapshot gating (merge queue / merge-bot synthesized tree) + the nightly-test-leg convergence (nightly keeps build/release legs, drops test legs once the snapshot run absorbs them) + subsuming the #1282 binaries-pr dispatch wiring into the snapshot gate. Owner directives 2026-10-05 recorded in the issue; that slice intentionally left out of this PR — it changes the merge flow itself, not the leg topology.
- N4-convergence caveat respected: nightly test legs are NOT touched here — until the merge-snapshot gate exists, the nightly full matrix stays main's backstop.

## Verification

Local dart is unavailable on this box (flutter shim cannot write its cache) — remote CI verifies. The workflow YAML is ruby-YAML validated, job ids/needs statically resolved, and the two new guard tests are pure text/YAML asserts runnable in the existing test-core shards. The legs themselves (macOS JS-engine run, linux/windows release builds, the filer's gh calls) get no local tests — they are CI-only surfaces, exercised by the first dispatch/nightly runs; the AC3 drill procedure is: `gh workflow run nightly.yml -f fileTracker=true` on a branch with a forced-failing leg, then expect the tracker comment inside that run.

Refs: #177, #1265, #1266, #466, #1220, #1280, #1282, #1364

Let me read AGENTS.md conventions first (it's huge — 132KB; let me look at relevant sections). Also I should check the repository structure for CI conventions.

Key review points to analyze:

1. **The `paths` step dispatch arm**: On `workflow_dispatch`, `BASE_REF`/`HEAD_REF` env vars come from `github.event.pull_request.base.sha` which will be empty on dispatch events. The script does:
```bash
if [ -z "$HEAD_REF" ]; then
  HEAD_REF="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
  BASE_REF="$(git merge-base origin/main "$HEAD_REF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  ...
fi
```

Concern: `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` on a checkout with fetch-depth: 0 — does origin/main exist? The checkout is of the head SHA via SM validation dispatch. Let me verify the checkout action in ci.yml — is it `fetch-depth: 0`? Also whether `ref` is checked out to the head SHA — `git rev-parse HEAD` works regardless.

An important subtlety: merge-base computes fork point with origin/main *at the time of checkout*. If the PR is behind main (e.g., main moved forward), merge-base still gives the common ancestor, which is correct for "what does this PR change relative to where it forked". But if the PR is stale and main has since incorporated conflicting changes, the merge-base diff may not represent the actual merged diff. That's an accepted approximation.

Another subtlety: on a dispatch event for a *main* branch run (e.g., push-emulated dispatch), merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) == HEAD → diff empty → exzone/locksmoke outputs not set → the legs skip. The PR description says "merge-base == HEAD (a main dispatch, or an already-merged branch) diffs to nothing and the narrowed arms skip." Is that desired? For main dispatches — the nightly covers them. OK, documented intent.

But wait — what about the SM validation dispatch on a head SHA? The changes job checks out... let me look at the full ci.yml changes job to see the checkout step. Need to confirm fetch-depth: 0 claim.

2. **Race condition / TOCTOU on merge-base**: If the head branch is rebased/merged after dispatch, the classifier's diff may differ from what the PR later merges. Accepted.

3. **The fail-safe branch**: on merge-base failure, sets exzone=true and locksmoke=true, exit 0. But NOTE: on `pull_request` events, if HEAD_REF is set (it is), the dispatch arm is skipped — good. But there's a subtle issue: on pull_request events where `github.event.pull_request.base.sha` is empty (rare), `git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF"` with empty BASE_REF would fail → `grep -qE` gets empty input → exzone/locksmoke outputs not set → legs skip. Fail-open instead of fail-safe on PR events. But that's pre-existing behavior for the PR-event arm (this arm previously existed for PR events). Actually the previous code had the same shape for the PR event; the exzone grep was in the same step. So not new. Minor.

4. **Escalation streak jq**: 
```bash
streak=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow nightly.yml \
  --event schedule --status completed --limit 10 \
  --json conclusion,databaseId \
  --jq 'reduce .[] as $r ({s: 0, done: false};
        if ($r.databaseId | tostring) == "'"$GITHUB_RUN_ID"'" or .done then .
        elif $r.conclusion == "failure" then {s: (.s + 1), done: false}
        else {s: .s, done: true} end) | .s')
```

Issues:
- `gh run list` returns runs in descending order (newest first). The reduce iterates newest → oldest. The current run is excluded, and after hitting the current run, `.done` is set? Wait — the condition: `if ($r.databaseId | tostring) == "'"$GITHUB_RUN_ID"'" or .done then .` — when it hits the current run OR done is already true, keep state unchanged. When it hits a failure → s+1. When non-failure → done: true. Since runs are newest-first and the current run is the newest, the current run is hit first, state unchanged (s stays 0, done stays false), then continues to older runs counting consecutive failures until the first non-failure. That works... IF the current run is in the list. But wait — the current run is a SCHEDULE run only in the schedule case. On a drill dispatch with fileTracker=true, `--event schedule` excludes the current run entirely — so the streak counts prior scheduled nights, which is exactly the documented intent ("dispatch runs never count").

  Hmm, but there's a subtlety: `--limit 10` — only the last 10 completed scheduled runs are considered. If more than 10 consecutive red nights, the streak caps at 10. Fine for escalation (>=1).

  Another subtlety: `gh run list --status completed` — the current run's *status* is in_progress while the job runs, so it wouldn't be returned anyway by `--status completed` filter. The databaseId exclusion is belt-and-braces. OK.

  One more: shell interpolation `'"$GITHUB_RUN_ID"'` inside the jq program — GITHUB_RUN_ID is set by the runner (numeric), so injection risk is minimal. It's a GitHub-provided env var. Fine.

  What about `--workflow nightly.yml`? gh run list accepts a workflow name or file name. OK.

  Edge: `gh run list` with `--event schedule` — supported flag. OK.

  Potential issue: `reduce` with initial `{s: 0, done: false}` — when the first element (newest) is NOT the current run (e.g., the run is a dispatch drill, or the current scheduled run is somehow not listed because it's still in progress), the reduce starts counting from the newest completed run. That's correct behavior.

  BUT: what if the current scheduled run IS listed as completed already (a fast filer job, run concluded by the time the API is queried)? The filer job is near the end of the workflow (needs full-quality etc.), and the run can't be "completed" while a job is running — `gh run list` reads the run status which is in_progress. Actually — the run concludes only after all jobs finish, including auto-issue. So the current run is in_progress; with `--status completed` it's not returned. The databaseId exclusion handles a hypothetical race. OK — good defensive coding.

  Edge: the workflow file name for scheduled runs — `--workflow nightly.yml` works if the schedule belongs to that workflow file. OK.

  Hmm — one real issue: `nights=$((streak + 1))` — on a drill dispatch (fileTracker=true), streak counts prior scheduled failures, and the label gets added if streak >= 1. So a drill on the day after 2 red nights would escalate the tracker with "3 consecutive red nights" even though the red was a synthetic drill. Hmm, actually, is that wrong? The drill deliberately arms the filer to file/comment. If there were real red nights before, escalating seems... acceptable? The body says "Consecutive red scheduled nights (incl. this one): N" — on a drill, "this one" is not a scheduled night, so the count is misleading. Minor — the escalation on a drill is arguably by-design (the drill arms the filer fully). But the comment "nights=$((streak + 1))" — on a drill dispatch where streak=0, nights=1, no escalation. If a drill runs after 1 red scheduled night, streak=1 → escalate. The escalated label description says "Nightly red 2+ consecutive scheduled nights". A drill red isn't a scheduled night. Edge case — the drill's purpose is to verify filing; escalation on drill is a minor false positive. Worth a SUGGESTION.

7. **Label creation on every red**: `gh label create nightly-red-escalated --force` — `--force` edits the label if it exists. OK, idempotent.

# rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          # ── Issue #1267 N1/N2 dispatch arm ──────────────────────────────
          # SM validation dispatches carry NO pull_request event context,
          # so BASE_REF/HEAD_REF are empty there: derive the validated diff
          # from git — merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) is the PR fork point
          # (the checkout above is fetch-depth: 0, so origin/main exists).
          # merge-base == HEAD (a main dispatch, or an already-merged
          # branch) diffs to nothing and the narrowed arms skip. A failed
          # resolve fails SAFE: both arms run unconditioned —
          # over-triggering a rare-path leg costs minutes, under-triggering
          # one hides a nightly-only red (the #1309 class).
          if [ -z "$HEAD_REF" ]; then
            HEAD_REF="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            BASE_REF="$(git merge-base origin/main "$HEAD_REF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [ -z "$BASE_REF" ]; then
              echo "::warning::merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) failed on the dispatch checkout — failing safe: exzone + locksmoke arms run"
              echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Gated on
          # BOTH pull_request events and SM validation dispatches (the
          # legs below consult these outputs on either event). Context:
          # the ubuntu flutter-tests leg runs this family but every
          # engine-dependent test SKIPS there (native_test_guard.dart finds
          # no QuickJS .so on a bare runner); they truly execute only on
          # macOS — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307). The issue's
          # packages/js_widget_runtime/** is an EXTERNAL repo now, so its
          # bumps arrive via the flutter_app/pubspec.yaml pin.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^flutter_app/lib/apps/|^lib/src/js_ext/|^flutter_app/test/apps/|^flutter_app/test/native_test_guard\.dart$|^flutter_app/pubspec\.yaml$)'; then
            echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N2 (AC2): the lockfile-refresh vector — resolution
          # floats transitive deps to latest-compatible, and the breaking
          # arrival (#1265: a transitive flutter_inappwebview) lands as a
          # flutter_app/pubspec.lock diff with nothing else changed. The
          # flutter-app-lock-smoke legs are the pre-merge net; PRs not
          # touching the lockfile never pay for them.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '^flutter_app/pubspec\.lock$'; then
            echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]; then
            # Dispatch done — the stages classifier below reads a
            # pull_request event's base/head only; on dispatches the group
            # outputs stay with the non-PR filter step (full gate).
            exit 0
          fi
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          case " $stages " in *"flutter"*) echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"test-core"*) echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"analyze"*) echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # Issue #551: test/integration changes select the mock-LLM leg.
          case " $stages " in *"integration-mock"*) echo "intmock=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # All nine stages selected = a shared/unknown path changed:
          if [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ]; then
            # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
            stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          fi
          if [ "$(echo $stages | wc -w)" -eq 9 ]; then
            echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #303: the #262 DoD perf gate must red-block the MERGE for
          # trajectory regressions, not only the release — before #551 the
          # only integration leg outside PRs was tag-time. The perf-gate
          # leg re-selects the same gate via --tags perf. Paths = everything
          # the #262 fix touched: ledger core, fa_ui trajectory widgets, CLI
          # trajectory parts, the fah entrypoint, its tests, and the app's
          # session load path.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^lib/src/trajectory/|^packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/|^lib/src/cli/trajectory_|^bin/fah\.dart$|^test/(integration/)?trajectory/|^flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service(_sessions)?\.dart$)'; then
            echo "perf=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # model_request_summary records and the session chain's shape —
          # a red usage-fold suite blocks the merge even when the regular
          # legs are green.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^lib/src/trajectory/|^lib/src/session/|^lib/src/usage/|^test/usage/|^lib/src/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger\.dart$)'; then
            echo "usagefold=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (issue #1267 N1 slice 2): ci.yml has NO pull_request
  # trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM workflow_dispatch on the head
  # SHA (machine-sm.yml). The changes classifier derives the validated diff
  # under BOTH events (merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) on dispatches), so
  # this leg is PATH-TRIGGERED: a PR touching only lib/src core never pays
  # for it (AC1), a lib/apps + js_ext diff does, and a classifier failure
  # fails safe (the leg runs). Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it —
  # the nightly flutter-app-macos leg stays the full-suite backstop there.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N2 (AC2) — lockfile-modified release smoke. Resolution
  # floats transitive deps to latest-compatible on every resolve, and the
  # breaking arrival (#1265: a transitive flutter_inappwebview nobody
  # declares) lands as a flutter_app/pubspec.lock diff — a surface the PR
  # legs never built: the native linux/windows desktop targets were
  # nightly-only (nightly.yml build-release), so the break surfaced as the
  # 5-red-nights window instead of a red PR. When the diff MODIFIES the
  # lockfile, this matrix release-builds the app on linux+windows pre-merge
  # (the same two targets the nightly carries); every other PR pays
  # nothing. The resolve rides the shared composite action (--enforce-
  # lockfile, #726 retry, skew fail-fast — test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_
  # test.dart), so a pubspec/lockfile skew fails HERE loudly before any
  # build step. Path-triggered like exzone: pull_request events AND SM
  # validation dispatches (merge-base diff in the classifier, fail-safe).
  # Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the nightly build-release
  # matrix stays the backstop, and a red leg reddens the required Quality
  # gate (platform class — it must block the merge, never the pure-Dart
  # publish, #1368).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-lock-smoke:
    name: Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.locksmoke == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
          - os: windows
            runner: windows-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Same pinned SDK as the nightly build-release legs (#281).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      # Linux desktop toolchain + plugin native deps (gtk3 for the runner,
      # gstreamer for audioplayers_linux) — same as the nightly linux leg.
      - name: Install Linux desktop toolchain
        if: matrix.os == 'linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y clang cmake ninja-build pkg-config \
            libgtk-3-dev liblzma-dev libstdc++-12-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Create placeholder firebase_options.dart
        shell: bash
        run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: flutter build ${{ matrix.os }} --release (lockfile smoke)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        shell: bash
        run: flutter build ${{ matrix.os }} --release

  # Issue #433: flutter_app CRAP ratchet — the app's beasts were never
  # gated (the root crap4dart.yaml covers core lib/bin only). The 2
  # flutter-tests shards above now emit --coverage; this job merges them
  # into ONE lcov (union DA hits, never cat — same as the core guards)
  # and runs the pinned crap4dart against flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
  # It is also the only home of the config guards: badge sync (AC1),
  # generated-exclude parity (E1) and the only-down git-history threshold
  # guard (AC3) — a raised threshold cannot merge, a new one (bootstrap)
  # can.
  app-crap-gate:
    name: Flutter app CRAP ratchet

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1457
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1457
- **Title**: ci(1267): path-triggered legs under dispatch-only CI (N1 AC1 + N2 lock-smoke) + nightly-red filer resurrection (N3)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1267-path-triggered-legs` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +597
- **Deletions**: -54
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T16:09:16Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T20:45:54Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1267 (slice 2 of the epic: N1/AC1 + N2/AC2 + N3/AC3; N4/AC5 remains, see Delivered vs remaining).

Motivating incidents, both CLOSED: #1265 (native build break arrived via an uncommitted lockfile — no PR surface at all) and #1266 (macOS app-suite regression whose only surface was nightly-only). AC4 linkage: both closed before this slice.

## Delivered

**N1/AC1 — path-triggered exclusion-zone leg under dispatch-only CI.** Slice 1 (#1350) landed `flutter-app-exzone` path-BLIND: it ran on EVERY SM validation dispatch because the `changes` classifier had no pull_request event to diff. This slice makes the classifier derive the validated diff itself: on `workflow_dispatch` it computes `merge-base(origin/main, HEAD)` (the PR fork point; the changes checkout is already fetch-depth: 0). A lib/src-only PR no longer pays for the macOS JS-engine leg; a `flutter_app/lib/apps/**` / `lib/src/js_ext/**` / exclusion-test diff does. Classification failure fails SAFE — the rare-path arms run unconditioned (over-triggering costs minutes; under-triggering hides a nightly-only red, the gh-1307/#1309 class). The four group outputs stay with the non-PR filter step, so main dispatches keep the full gate.

**N2/AC2 — lockfile-modified release smoke.** Lockfile committed + `--enforce-lockfile` everywhere already landed (gh-1296/gh-1265). Missing piece: the native linux/windows desktop targets were nightly-only, so a lockfile float (#1265's transitive `flutter_inappwebview`) had no pre-merge surface. New `flutter-app-lock-smoke` matrix (ubuntu + windows) runs `flutter build linux|windows --release` ONLY when the diff modifies `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` — same path-triggered model as exzone, same pinned SDK (`3.47.x`) and Linux toolchain as the nightly build-release legs. The resolve rides the shared `--enforce-lockfile` composite action (#726 retry + skew fail-fast), so a pubspec/lockfile skew fails loudly before any build. A red smoke reddens the required `Quality gate` (platform class per #1368: blocks the merge, never the pure-Dart publish). PRs not touching the lockfile pay nothing.

**N3/AC3 — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation.** Root cause of five silent red nights (last living tracker #466): the dedup lookup read jq's literal `"null"` (empty result of bare `.[0].number`) as a truthy issue number and died commenting issue `"null"` — never filing. Fixed with `.[0].number // empty` in BOTH steps (the shape ci.yml's ci-red-report already uses). Additionally:
- the job arms on `schedule` AND on a new `fileTracker=true` workflow_dispatch input — the AC3 synthetic-red drill (dispatch a forced-failing nightly with the flag → tracker filed/commented within the same run); manual dispatches without the flag stay tracker-silent;
- close-on-green stays schedule-only (a drill dispatch is not a night and must not close the live tracker);
- the decision — filed / commented / closed / why-not — is logged to the job output AND the step summary on every run (an empty decision log is how the filer stayed dead);
- two consecutive red SCHEDULED nights add `nightly-red-escalated` (streak = completed schedule-event failures before this run, current run excluded, dispatch runs never count; green resets naturally).

Note on #1364: that card is the `flake_watch.py` `--search`-based dedup (unquoted `(#<digits>` title fragment) — a DIFFERENT dedup in DIFFERENT code; untouched here, as scoped. The nightly filer's dedup is label-scoped JSON + jq, immune to the search-quoting class.

**Guards.** `test/ci_1267_path_triggered_legs_test.dart` + `test/nightly_filer_1267_test.dart` pin the wiring (structural lint over the workflow YAML — the repo's static-assert pattern, cf. `ci_binaries_arch_gate_test.dart`); `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart` AC3 count 12 → 13 for the new leg's action use (documented in place).

## Delivered vs remaining (issue ACs)

- AC1 ✅ (path-triggered on both events; a PR touching the external `packages/js_widget_runtime/` arrives as a `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin → exzone runs; lib/src-only → skips)
- AC2 ✅ (lock-smoke on lockfile diff; not touching → skipped)
- AC3 ✅ (filer resurrection + drill flag + decision log + escalation — verified by the drill dispatch once CI runs; remote-only surface)
- AC4 ✅ both incidents closed (linked above)
- AC5 / N4 ❌ remaining: merge-snapshot gating (merge queue / merge-bot synthesized tree) + the nightly-test-leg convergence (nightly keeps build/release legs, drops test legs once the snapshot run absorbs them) + subsuming the #1282 binaries-pr dispatch wiring into the snapshot gate. Owner directives 2026-10-05 recorded in the issue; that slice intentionally left out of this PR — it changes the merge flow itself, not the leg topology.
- N4-convergence caveat respected: nightly test legs are NOT touched here — until the merge-snapshot gate exists, the nightly full matrix stays main's backstop.

## Verification

Local dart is unavailable on this box (flutter shim cannot write its cache) — remote CI verifies. The workflow YAML is ruby-YAML validated, job ids/needs statically resolved, and the two new guard tests are pure text/YAML asserts runnable in the existing test-core shards. The legs themselves (macOS JS-engine run, linux/windows release builds, the filer's gh calls) get no local tests — they are CI-only surfaces, exercised by the first dispatch/nightly runs; the AC3 drill procedure is: `gh workflow run nightly.yml -f fileTracker=true` on a branch with a forced-failing leg, then expect the tracker comment inside that run.

Refs: #177, #1265, #1266, #466, #1220, #1280, #1282, #1364

Key review points to analyze:

1. **The `paths` step dispatch arm**: On `workflow_dispatch`, `BASE_REF`/`HEAD_REF` env vars come from `github.event.pull_request.base.sha` which will be empty on dispatch events. The script does:
```bash
if [ -z "$HEAD_REF" ]; then
  HEAD_REF="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
  BASE_REF="$(git merge-base origin/main "$HEAD_REF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  ...
fi
```

Concern: `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` on a checkout with fetch-depth: 0 — does origin/main exist? The checkout is of the head SHA via SM validation dispatch. Let me verify the checkout action in ci.yml — is it `fetch-depth: 0`? Also whether `ref` is checked out to the head SHA — `git rev-parse HEAD` works regardless.

An important subtlety: merge-base computes fork point with origin/main *at the time of checkout*. If the PR is behind main (e.g., main moved forward), merge-base still gives the common ancestor, which is correct for "what does this PR change relative to where it forked". But if the PR is stale and main has since incorporated conflicting changes, the merge-base diff may not represent the actual merged diff. That's an accepted approximation.

Another subtlety: on a dispatch event for a *main* branch run (e.g., push-emulated dispatch), merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) == HEAD → diff empty → exzone/locksmoke outputs not set → the legs skip. The PR description says "merge-base == HEAD (a main dispatch, or an already-merged branch) diffs to nothing and the narrowed arms skip." Is that desired? For main dispatches — the nightly covers them. OK, documented intent.

But wait — what about the SM validation dispatch on a head SHA? The changes job checks out... let me look at the full ci.yml changes job to see the checkout step. Need to confirm fetch-depth: 0 claim.

2. **Race condition / TOCTOU on merge-base**: If the head branch is rebased/merged after dispatch, the classifier's diff may differ from what the PR later merges. Accepted.

3. **The fail-safe branch**: on merge-base failure, sets exzone=true and locksmoke=true, exit 0. But NOTE: on `pull_request` events, if HEAD_REF is set (it is), the dispatch arm is skipped — good. But there's a subtle issue: on pull_request events where `github.event.pull_request.base.sha` is empty (rare), `git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF"` with empty BASE_REF would fail → `grep -qE` gets empty input → exzone/locksmoke outputs not set → legs skip. Fail-open instead of fail-safe on PR events. But that's pre-existing behavior for the PR-event arm (this arm previously existed for PR events). Actually the previous code had the same shape for the PR event; the exzone grep was in the same step. So not new. Minor.

4. **Escalation streak jq**: 
```bash
streak=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow nightly.yml \
  --event schedule --status completed --limit 10 \
  --json conclusion,databaseId \
  --jq 'reduce .[] as $r ({s: 0, done: false};
        if ($r.databaseId | tostring) == "'"$GITHUB_RUN_ID"'" or .done then .
        elif $r.conclusion == "failure" then {s: (.s + 1), done: false}
        else {s: .s, done: true} end) | .s')
```

- `gh run list` returns runs in descending order (newest first). The reduce iterates newest → oldest. The current run is excluded, and after hitting the current run, `.done` is set? Wait — the condition: `if ($r.databaseId | tostring) == "'"$GITHUB_RUN_ID"'" or .done then .` — when it hits the current run OR done is already true, keep state unchanged. When it hits a failure → s+1. When non-failure → done: true.         env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          # ── Issue #1267 N1/N2 dispatch arm ──────────────────────────────
          # SM validation dispatches carry NO pull_request event context,
          # so BASE_REF/HEAD_REF are empty there: derive the validated diff
          # from git — merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) is the PR fork point
          # (the checkout above is fetch-depth: 0, so origin/main exists).
          # merge-base == HEAD (a main dispatch, or an already-merged
          # branch) diffs to nothing and the narrowed arms skip. A failed
          # resolve fails SAFE: both arms run unconditioned —
          # over-triggering a rare-path leg costs minutes, under-triggering
          # one hides a nightly-only red (the #1309 class).
          if [ -z "$HEAD_REF" ]; then
            HEAD_REF="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            BASE_REF="$(git merge-base origin/main "$HEAD_REF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [ -z "$BASE_REF" ]; then
              echo "::warning::merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) failed on the dispatch checkout — failing safe: exzone + locksmoke arms run"
              echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Gated on
          # BOTH pull_request events and SM validation dispatches (the
          # legs below consult these outputs on either event). Context:
          # the ubuntu flutter-tests leg runs this family but every
          # engine-dependent test SKIPS there (native_test_guard.dart finds
          # no QuickJS .so on a bare runner); they truly execute only on
          # macOS — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307). The issue's
          # packages/js_widget_runtime/** is an EXTERNAL repo now, so its
          # bumps arrive via the flutter_app/pubspec.yaml pin.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^flutter_app/lib/apps/|^lib/src/js_ext/|^flutter_app/test/apps/|^flutter_app/test/native_test_guard\.dart$|^flutter_app/pubspec\.yaml$)'; then

          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |

            # Dispatch done — the stages classifier below reads a

  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (issue #1267 N1 slice 2): ci.yml has NO pull_request
  # trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM workflow_dispatch on the head
  # SHA (machine-sm.yml). The changes classifier derives the validated diff
  # under BOTH events (merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) on dispatches), so
  # this leg is PATH-TRIGGERED: a PR touching only lib/src core never pays
  # for it (AC1), a lib/apps + js_ext diff does, and a classifier failure
  # fails safe (the leg runs). Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it —
  # the nightly flutter-app-macos leg stays the full-suite backstop there.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N2 (AC2) — lockfile-modified release smoke. Resolution
  # floats transitive deps to latest-compatible on every resolve, and the
  # breaking arrival (#1265: a transitive flutter_inappwebview nobody
  # declares) lands as a flutter_app/pubspec.lock diff — a surface the PR
  # legs never built: the native linux/windows desktop targets were
  # nightly-only (nightly.yml build-release), so the break surfaced as the
  # 5-red-nights window instead of a red PR. When the diff MODIFIES the
  # lockfile, this matrix release-builds the app on linux+windows pre-merge
  # (the same two targets the nightly carries); every other PR pays
  # nothing. The resolve rides the shared composite action (--enforce-
  # lockfile, #726 retry, skew fail-fast — test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_
  # test.dart), so a pubspec/lockfile skew fails HERE loudly before any
  # build step. Path-triggered like exzone: pull_request events AND SM
  # validation dispatches (merge-base diff in the classifier, fail-safe).
  # Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the nightly build-release
  # matrix stays the backstop, and a red leg reddens the required Quality
  # gate (platform class — it must block the merge, never the pure-Dart
  # publish, #1368).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-lock-smoke:
    name: Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.locksmoke == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
          - os: windows
            runner: windows-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Same pinned SDK as the nightly build-release legs (#281).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      # Linux desktop toolchain + plugin native deps (gtk3 for the runner,
      # gstreamer for audioplayers_linux) — same as the nightly linux leg.
      - name: Install Linux desktop toolchain
        if: matrix.os == 'linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y clang cmake ninja-build pkg-config \
            libgtk-3-dev liblzma-dev libstdc++-12-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Create placeholder firebase_options.dart
        shell: bash

build-release:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} (release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: macos
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build macos --release
          - target: ios
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build ios --release --no-codesign
          - target: android
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build apk --flavor store --release
          - target: web
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build web --release
          - target: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build linux --release
          - target: windows
            runner: windows-latest
            cmd: flutter build windows --release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Same pinned SDK as the PR build legs and the release path (#281).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        if: matrix.target == 'android'
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      # Linux desktop toolchain + plugin native deps (gtk3 for the runner,
      # gstreamer for audioplayers_linux).
      - name: Install Linux desktop toolchain
        if: matrix.target == 'linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y clang cmake ninja-build pkg-config \
            libgtk-3-dev liblzma-dev libstdc++-12-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Create placeholder firebase_options.dart
        shell: bash
        run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # bf81411e made Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist a hard build input
      # (Runner resources + Crashlytics dSYM-phase inputPaths); the real
      # file is gitignored and written from a release secret these legs
      # don't have — seed the same placeholder as the ci.yml PR legs.
      - name: Write placeholder GoogleService-Info.plist (Apple targets)
        if: matrix.target == 'ios' || matrix.target == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          BUNDLE_ID="dev.fa1.${{ matrix.target }}"

      - name: ${{ matrix.cmd }}

  # Files ONE deduped issue when the scheduled nightly run goes red: the
  # open `nightly-red` issue is searched first and only commented on, so a
  # persistent failure never spams duplicates. A GREEN scheduled run closes
  # the open issue (the nightly-red tracker is only as good as its sunset).
  #
  # Resurrection (issue #1267 N3): five consecutive red nights
  # (2026-10-01 → 10-05) filed NOTHING. Two defects, both fixed here —
  #  1. the dedup lookup read jq's literal "null" (an empty result of
  #     `.[0].number`) as a truthy issue number, so the no-open-tracker
  #     path died commenting issue "null" and never filed — every lookup
  #     now reads `.[0].number // empty` (both steps);
  #  2. the job was schedule-only, so the AC3 synthetic-red drill could
  #     not reach it — dispatch + fileTracker=true arms it too.
  # The decision (filed / commented / closed / why-not) lands in the job
  # output AND the step summary; two consecutive red scheduled nights add
  # the nightly-red-escalated label (streak counted from the completed
  # schedule-event runs preceding this one — dispatch runs never count).
  auto-issue:
    name: File nightly-red issue
    needs: [full-quality, pty-integration, cli-visual, flutter-app-macos, build-release]
    if: >-
      always() && !cancelled() &&
      (github.event_name == 'schedule' ||
       (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.fileTracker == 'true'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      # issues: write — file/comment/close/label the deduped nightly-red
      # issue. actions: read — the filing leg lists this run's jobs via
      # `gh api repos/.../actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs` and the escalation
      # streak via `gh run list`; a job-level permissions block drops
      # every unlisted scope to none, so without this the calls 403
      # ("Resource not accessible by integration") and no issue is filed.
      issues: write
      actions: read
    steps:
      # AC3 decision-log visibility: the arm/disarm reason is in the job
      # output on EVERY run, red or green, filing or not.
      - name: Filer decision (why-not visibility, #1267 AC3)
        if: always()
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "schedule" ]; then
            echo "filer armed: scheduled run — files/comments/closes the tracker"
          elif [ "${{ github.event.inputs.fileTracker }}" = "true" ]; then
            echo "filer armed: dispatch with fileTracker=true (AC3 synthetic-red drill)"
          else
            echo "filer decision: why-not — manual dispatch without fileTracker=true; pass it to exercise the tracker (AC3 drill)"
          fi

      - name: Close the nightly-red issue on a green run
        # Schedule-only: a manual (drill) dispatch is not a night — its
        # green must never close the live nightly tracker.
        if: success() && github.event_name == 'schedule'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          # `// empty` (issue #1267 N3): an empty result must read EMPTY —
          # jq's bare `.[0].number` prints the literal string "null",
          # which `[ -n ]` treats as a live issue number, so the close
          # died commenting issue "null" (the silent-death bug).
          existing=$(gh issue list --state open --label nightly-red \
            --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty' --repo "$repo")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
              --body "Green again: ${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID} — closing."
            gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo"
            echo "decision: closed #$existing — nightly green again"
            echo "decision: closed #$existing — nightly green again" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "decision: why-not close — no open nightly-red tracker"
            echo "decision: why-not close — no open nightly-red tracker" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      - name: Create or update the nightly-red issue
        if: failure()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          date=$(date -u +%F)
          title="Nightly full-matrix red: ${date}"
          repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          gh label create nightly-red --force \
            --description "Nightly full-quality run is failing" \
            --color B60205 --repo "$repo"
          gh label create nightly-red-escalated --force \
            --description "Nightly red 2+ consecutive scheduled nights (issue #1267 N3)" \
            --color D93F0B --repo "$repo"
          # Failing job names of this run, plus the run URL.
          failing=$(gh api \
            "repos/$repo/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          [ -z "$failing" ] && failing="(unknown)"
          # N3 escalation: consecutive red SCHEDULED nights completed
          # BEFORE this run (this run's own red is the +1). The streak
          # stops at the first non-failure. Dispatch runs never count —
          # the label tracks real nights.
          streak=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow nightly.yml \
            --event schedule --status completed --limit 10 \
            --json conclusion,databaseId \
            --jq 'reduce .[] as $r ({s: 0, done: false};
                  if ($r.databaseId | tostring) == "'"$GITHUB_RUN_ID"'" or .done then .
                  elif $r.conclusion == "failure" then {s: (.s + 1), done: false}
                  else {s: .s, done: true} end) | .s')
          nights=$((streak + 1))
          echo "decision: red night ${nights} in a row (streak input: ${streak} completed failures)"
          body=$(printf 'Nightly full-matrix run is red.\n\nFailing jobs: %s\nRun: %s\nConsecutive red scheduled nights (incl. this one): %s\n' \
            "$failing" "${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" "$nights")
          # Dedup: comment on the existing open nightly-red issue instead of
          # opening a duplicate. --repo everywhere: this job has no checkout,
          # bare `gh` invokes git for repo detection and dies with
          # "not a git repository" (the 2026-09-18 filing-leg failure).
          # `// empty` on the lookup — the literal-"null" bug above.
          existing=$(gh issue list --state open --label nightly-red \
            --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty' --repo "$repo")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --body "$body" --repo "$repo"
            echo "decision: commented the open tracker #$existing (no duplicate filed)"
            echo "decision: commented the open tracker #$existing (no duplicate filed)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            target="$existing"
          else
            target=$(gh issue create --title "$title" --label nightly-red \
              --body "$body" --assignee ai-teammate --repo "$repo")
            echo "decision: filed $target"
            echo "decision: filed $target" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
          if [ "$streak" -ge 1 ]; then
            gh issue edit "$target" --add-label nightly-red-escalated --repo "$repo"
            echo "decision: escalated $target — $nights consecutive red scheduled nights"
            echo "decision: escalated $target — $nights consecutive red scheduled nights" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. - **State**: open

- **Additions**: +597
- **Deletions**: -54
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T16:09:16Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T20:45:54Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1267 (slice 2 of the epic: N1/AC1 + N2/AC2 + N3/AC3; N4/AC5 remains, see Delivered vs remaining).

Motivating incidents, both CLOSED: #1265 (native build break arrived via an uncommitted lockfile — no PR surface at all) and #1266 (macOS app-suite regression whose only surface was nightly-only). AC4 linkage: both closed before this slice.

## Delivered

**N1/AC1 — path-triggered exclusion-zone leg under dispatch-only CI.** Slice 1 (#1350) landed `flutter-app-exzone` path-BLIND: it ran on EVERY SM validation dispatch because the `changes` classifier had no pull_request event to diff. This slice makes the classifier derive the validated diff itself: on `workflow_dispatch` it computes `merge-base(origin/main, HEAD)` (the PR fork point; the changes checkout is already fetch-depth: 0). A lib/src-only PR no longer pays for the macOS JS-engine leg; a `flutter_app/lib/apps/**` / `lib/src/js_ext/**` / exclusion-test diff does. Classification failure fails SAFE — the rare-path arms run unconditioned (over-triggering costs minutes; under-triggering hides a nightly-only red, the gh-1307/#1309 class). The four group outputs stay with the non-PR filter step, so main dispatches keep the full gate.

**N2/AC2 — lockfile-modified release smoke.** Lockfile committed + `--enforce-lockfile` everywhere already landed (gh-1296/gh-1265). Missing piece: the native linux/windows desktop targets were nightly-only, so a lockfile float (#1265's transitive `flutter_inappwebview`) had no pre-merge surface. New `flutter-app-lock-smoke` matrix (ubuntu + windows) runs `flutter build linux|windows --release` ONLY when the diff modifies `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` — same path-triggered model as exzone, same pinned SDK (`3.47.x`) and Linux toolchain as the nightly build-release legs. The resolve rides the shared `--enforce-lockfile` composite action (#726 retry + skew fail-fast), so a pubspec/lockfile skew fails loudly before any build. A red smoke reddens the required `Quality gate` (platform class per #1368: blocks the merge, never the pure-Dart publish). PRs not touching the lockfile pay nothing.

**N3/AC3 — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation.** Root cause of five silent red nights (last living tracker #466): the dedup lookup read jq's literal `"null"` (empty result of bare `.[0].number`) as a truthy issue number and died commenting issue `"null"` — never filing. Fixed with `.[0].number // empty` in BOTH steps (the shape ci.yml's ci-red-report already uses). Additionally:
- the job arms on `schedule` AND on a new `fileTracker=true` workflow_dispatch input — the AC3 synthetic-red drill (dispatch a forced-failing nightly with the flag → tracker filed/commented within the same run); manual dispatches without the flag stay tracker-silent;
- close-on-green stays schedule-only (a drill dispatch is not a night and must not close the live tracker);
- the decision — filed / commented / closed / why-not — is logged to the job output AND the step summary on every run (an empty decision log is how the filer stayed dead);
- two consecutive red SCHEDULED nights add `nightly-red-escalated` (streak = completed schedule-event failures before this run, current run excluded, dispatch runs never count; green resets naturally).

Note on #1364: that card is the `flake_watch.py` `--search`-based dedup (unquoted `(#<digits>` title fragment) — a DIFFERENT dedup in DIFFERENT code; untouched here, as scoped. The nightly filer's dedup is label-scoped JSON + jq, immune to the search-quoting class.

**Guards.** `test/ci_1267_path_triggered_legs_test.dart` + `test/nightly_filer_1267_test.dart` pin the wiring (structural lint over the workflow YAML — the repo's static-assert pattern, cf. `ci_binaries_arch_gate_test.dart`); `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart` AC3 count 12 → 13 for the new leg's action use (documented in place).

## Delivered vs remaining (issue ACs)

- AC1 ✅ (path-triggered on both events; a PR touching the external `packages/js_widget_runtime/` arrives as a `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin → exzone runs; lib/src-only → skips)
- AC2 ✅ (lock-smoke on lockfile diff; not touching → skipped)
- AC3 ✅ (filer resurrection + drill flag + decision log + escalation — verified by the drill dispatch once CI runs; remote-only surface)
- AC4 ✅ both incidents closed (linked above)
- AC5 / N4 ❌ remaining: merge-snapshot gating (merge queue / merge-bot synthesized tree) + the nightly-test-leg convergence (nightly keeps build/release legs, drops test legs once the snapshot run absorbs them) + subsuming the #1282 binaries-pr dispatch wiring into the snapshot gate. Owner directives 2026-10-05 recorded in the issue; that slice intentionally left out of this PR — it changes the merge flow itself, not the leg topology.
- N4-convergence caveat respected: nightly test legs are NOT touched here — until the merge-snapshot gate exists, the nightly full matrix stays main's backstop.

## Verification

Local dart is unavailable on this box (flutter shim cannot write its cache) — remote CI verifies. The workflow YAML is ruby-YAML validated, job ids/needs statically resolved, and the two new guard tests are pure text/YAML asserts runnable in the existing test-core shards. The legs themselves (macOS JS-engine run, linux/windows release builds, the filer's gh calls) get no local tests — they are CI-only surfaces, exercised by the first dispatch/nightly runs; the AC3 drill procedure is: `gh workflow run nightly.yml -f fileTracker=true` on a branch with a forced-failing leg, then expect the tracker comment inside that run.

An important subtlety: merge-base computes fork point with origin/main *at the time of checkout*. If the PR is behind main (e.g., main moved forward), merge-base still gives the common ancestor, which is correct for "what does this PR change relative to where it forked". But if the PR is stale and main has since incorporated conflicting changes, the merge-base diff may not represent the actual merged diff. That's an accepted approximation.

Another subtlety: on a dispatch event for a *main* branch run (e.g., push-emulated dispatch), merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) == HEAD → diff empty → exzone/locksmoke outputs not set → the legs skip. name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']

  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also

# (missing/untracked/gitignored lockfiles) is enforced in ci.yml
      # Static gates, not here.
      - name: Lockfile gate (gh-1296 NG1/NG3)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        shell: bash

      - name: ${{ matrix.cmd }}
        working-directory: flutter_app
        shell: bash
        run: ${{ matrix.cmd }}

  # Files ONE deduped issue when the scheduled nightly run goes red: the
  # open `nightly-red` issue is searched first and only commented on, so a
  # persistent failure never spams duplicates. A GREEN scheduled run closes
  # the open issue (the nightly-red tracker is only as good as its sunset).
  #
  # Resurrection (issue #1267 N3): five consecutive red nights
  # (2026-10-01 → 10-05) filed NOTHING. Two defects, both fixed here —
  #  1. the dedup lookup read jq's literal "null" (an empty result of
  #     `.[0].number`) as a truthy issue number, so the no-open-tracker
  #     path died commenting issue "null" and never filed — every lookup
  #     now reads `.[0].number // empty` (both steps);
  #  2. the job was schedule-only, so the AC3 synthetic-red drill could
  #     not reach it — dispatch + fileTracker=true arms it too.
  # The decision (filed / commented / closed / why-not) lands in the job
  # output AND the step summary; two consecutive red scheduled nights add
  # the nightly-red-escalated label (streak counted from the completed
  # schedule-event runs preceding this one — dispatch runs never count).
  auto-issue:
    name: File nightly-red issue
    needs: [full-quality, pty-integration, cli-visual, flutter-app-macos, build-release]
    if: >-
      always() && !cancelled() &&
      (github.event_name == 'schedule' ||
       (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.fileTracker == 'true'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      # issues: write — file/comment/close/label the deduped nightly-red
      # issue. actions: read — the filing leg lists this run's jobs via
      # `gh api repos/.../actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs` and the escalation
      # streak via `gh run list`; a job-level permissions block drops
      # every unlisted scope to none, so without this the calls 403
      # ("Resource not accessible by integration") and no issue is filed.
      issues: write
      actions: read
    steps:
      # AC3 decision-log visibility: the arm/disarm reason is in the job
      # output on EVERY run, red or green, filing or not.
      - name: Filer decision (why-not visibility, #1267 AC3)
        if: always()
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "schedule" ]; then
            echo "filer armed: scheduled run — files/comments/closes the tracker"
          elif [ "${{ github.event.inputs.fileTracker }}" = "true" ]; then
            echo "filer armed: dispatch with fileTracker=true (AC3 synthetic-red drill)"
          else
            echo "filer decision: why-not — manual dispatch without fileTracker=true; pass it to exercise the tracker (AC3 drill)"
          fi

      - name: Close the nightly-red issue on a green run
        # Schedule-only: a manual (drill) dispatch is not a night — its
        # green must never close the live nightly tracker.
        if: success() && github.event_name == 'schedule'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          # `// empty` (issue #1267 N3): an empty result must read EMPTY —
          # jq's bare `.[0].number` prints the literal string "null",
          # which `[ -n ]` treats as a live issue number, so the close
          # died commenting issue "null" (the silent-death bug).
          existing=$(gh issue list --state open --label nightly-red \
            --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty' --repo "$repo")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
              --body "Green again: ${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID} — closing."
            gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo"
            echo "decision: closed #$existing — nightly green again"
            echo "decision: closed #$existing — nightly green again" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "decision: why-not close — no open nightly-red tracker"
            echo "decision: why-not close — no open nightly-red tracker" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      - name: Create or update the nightly-red issue
        if: failure()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          date=$(date -u +%F)
          title="Nightly full-matrix red: ${date}"
          repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          gh label create nightly-red --force \
            --description "Nightly full-quality run is failing" \
            --color B60205 --repo "$repo"
          gh label create nightly-red-escalated --force \
            --description "Nightly red 2+ consecutive scheduled nights (issue #1267 N3)" \
            --color D93F0B --repo "$repo"
          # Failing job names of this run, plus the run URL.
          failing=$(gh api \
            "repos/$repo/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          [ -z "$failing" ] && failing="(unknown)"
          # N3 escalation: consecutive red SCHEDULED nights completed
          # BEFORE this run (this run's own red is the +1). The streak
          # stops at the first non-failure. Dispatch runs never count —
          # the label tracks real nights.
          streak=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow nightly.yml \
            --event schedule --status completed --limit 10 \
            --json conclusion,databaseId \
            --jq 'reduce .[] as $r ({s: 0, done: false};
                  if ($r.databaseId | tostring) == "'"$GITHUB_RUN_ID"'" or .done then .
                  elif $r.conclusion == "failure" then {s: (.s + 1), done: false}
                  else {s: .s, done: true} end) | .s')
          nights=$((streak + 1))
          echo "decision: red night ${nights} in a row (streak input: ${streak} completed failures)"
          body=$(printf 'Nightly full-matrix run is red.\n\nFailing jobs: %s\nRun: %s\nConsecutive red scheduled nights (incl. this one): %s\n' \
            "$failing" "${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" "$nights")
          # Dedup: comment on the existing open nightly-red issue instead of
          # opening a duplicate. --repo everywhere: this job has no checkout,
          # bare `gh` invokes git for repo detection and dies with
          # "not a git repository" (the 2026-09-18 filing-leg failure).
          # `// empty` on the lookup — the literal-"null" bug above.
          existing=$(gh issue list --state open --label nightly-red \
            --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty' --repo "$repo")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --body "$body" --repo "$repo"
            echo "decision: commented the open tracker #$existing (no duplicate filed)"
            echo "decision: commented the open tracker #$existing (no duplicate filed)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            target="$existing"
          else
            target=$(gh issue create --title "$title" --label nightly-red \
              --body "$body" --assignee ai-teammate --repo "$repo")
            echo "decision: filed $target"
            echo "decision: filed $target" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
          if [ "$streak" -ge 1 ]; then
            gh issue edit "$target" --add-label nightly-red-escalated --repo "$repo"
            echo "decision: escalated $target — $nights consecutive red scheduled nights"
            echo "decision: escalated $target — $nights consecutive red scheduled nights" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
