# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1457
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1457
- **Title**: ci(1267): path-triggered legs under dispatch-only CI (N1 AC1 + N2 lock-smoke) + nightly-red filer resurrection (N3)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1267-path-triggered-legs` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +597
- **Deletions**: -54
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T16:09:16Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T20:45:54Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1267 (slice 2 of the epic: N1/AC1 + N2/AC2 + N3/AC3; N4/AC5 remains, see Delivered vs remaining).

Motivating incidents, both CLOSED: #1265 (native build break arrived via an uncommitted lockfile — no PR surface at all) and #1266 (macOS app-suite regression whose only surface was nightly-only). AC4 linkage: both closed before this slice.

## Delivered

**N1/AC1 — path-triggered exclusion-zone leg under dispatch-only CI.** Slice 1 (#1350) landed `flutter-app-exzone` path-BLIND: it ran on EVERY SM validation dispatch because the `changes` classifier had no pull_request event to diff. This slice makes the classifier derive the validated diff itself: on `workflow_dispatch` it computes `merge-base(origin/main, HEAD)` (the PR fork point; the changes checkout is already fetch-depth: 0). A lib/src-only PR no longer pays for the macOS JS-engine leg; a `flutter_app/lib/apps/**` / `lib/src/js_ext/**` / exclusion-test diff does. Classification failure fails SAFE — the rare-path arms run unconditioned (over-triggering costs minutes; under-triggering hides a nightly-only red, the gh-1307/#1309 class). The four group outputs stay with the non-PR filter step, so main dispatches keep the full gate.

**N2/AC2 — lockfile-modified release smoke.** Lockfile committed + `--enforce-lockfile` everywhere already landed (gh-1296/gh-1265). Missing piece: the native linux/windows desktop targets were nightly-only, so a lockfile float (#1265's transitive `flutter_inappwebview`) had no pre-merge surface. New `flutter-app-lock-smoke` matrix (ubuntu + windows) runs `flutter build linux|windows --release` ONLY when the diff modifies `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` — same path-triggered model as exzone, same pinned SDK (`3.47.x`) and Linux toolchain as the nightly build-release legs. The resolve rides the shared `--enforce-lockfile` composite action (#726 retry + skew fail-fast), so a pubspec/lockfile skew fails loudly before any build. A red smoke reddens the required `Quality gate` (platform class per #1368: blocks the merge, never the pure-Dart publish). PRs not touching the lockfile pay nothing.

**N3/AC3 — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation.** Root cause of five silent red nights (last living tracker #466): the dedup lookup read jq's literal `"null"` (empty result of bare `.[0].number`) as a truthy issue number and died commenting issue `"null"` — never filing. Fixed with `.[0].number // empty` in BOTH steps (the shape ci.yml's ci-red-report already uses). Additionally:
- the job arms on `schedule` AND on a new `fileTracker=true` workflow_dispatch input — the AC3 synthetic-red drill (dispatch a forced-failing nightly with the flag → tracker filed/commented within the same run); manual dispatches without the flag stay tracker-silent;
- close-on-green stays schedule-only (a drill dispatch is not a night and must not close the live tracker);
- the decision — filed / commented / closed / why-not — is logged to the job output AND the step summary on every run (an empty decision log is how the filer stayed dead);
- two consecutive red SCHEDULED nights add `nightly-red-escalated` (streak = completed schedule-event failures before this run, current run excluded, dispatch runs never count; green resets naturally).

Note on #1364: that card is the `flake_watch.py` `--search`-based dedup (unquoted `(#<digits>` title fragment) — a DIFFERENT dedup in DIFFERENT code; untouched here, as scoped. The nightly filer's dedup is label-scoped JSON + jq, immune to the search-quoting class.

**Guards.** `test/ci_1267_path_triggered_legs_test.dart` + `test/nightly_filer_1267_test.dart` pin the wiring (structural lint over the workflow YAML — the repo's static-assert pattern, cf. `ci_binaries_arch_gate_test.dart`); `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart` AC3 count 12 → 13 for the new leg's action use (documented in place).

## Delivered vs remaining (issue ACs)

- AC1 ✅ (path-triggered on both events; a PR touching the external `packages/js_widget_runtime/` arrives as a `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin → exzone runs; lib/src-only → skips)
- AC2 ✅ (lock-smoke on lockfile diff; not touching → skipped)
- AC3 ✅ (filer resurrection + drill flag + decision log + escalation — verified by the drill dispatch once CI runs; remote-only surface)
- AC4 ✅ both incidents closed (linked above)
- AC5 / N4 ❌ remaining: merge-snapshot gating (merge queue / merge-bot synthesized tree) + the nightly-test-leg convergence (nightly keeps build/release legs, drops test legs once the snapshot run absorbs them) + subsuming the #1282 binaries-pr dispatch wiring into the snapshot gate. Owner directives 2026-10-05 recorded in the issue; that slice intentionally left out of this PR — it changes the merge flow itself, not the leg topology.
- N4-convergence caveat respected: nightly test legs are NOT touched here — until the merge-snapshot gate exists, the nightly full matrix stays main's backstop.

## Verification

Local dart is unavailable on this box (flutter shim cannot write its cache) — remote CI verifies. The workflow YAML is ruby-YAML validated, job ids/needs statically resolved, and the two new guard tests are pure text/YAML asserts runnable in the existing test-core shards. The legs themselves (macOS JS-engine run, linux/windows release builds, the filer's gh calls) get no local tests — they are CI-only surfaces, exercised by the first dispatch/nightly runs; the AC3 drill procedure is: `gh workflow run nightly.yml -f fileTracker=true` on a branch with a forced-failing leg, then expect the tracker comment inside that run.

Refs: #177, #1265, #1266, #466, #1220, #1280, #1282, #1364

if [ -z "$HEAD_REF" ]; then

Let me verify the checkout action in ci.yml — is it `fetch-depth: 0`? Also whether `ref` is checked out to the head SHA — `git rev-parse HEAD` works regardless.

An important subtlety: merge-base computes fork point with origin/main *at the time of checkout*. If the PR is behind main (e.g., main moved forward), merge-base still gives the common ancestor, which is correct for "what does this PR change relative to where it forked". But if the PR is stale and main has since incorporated conflicting changes, the merge-base diff may not represent the actual merged diff. That's an accepted approximation.

Another subtlety: on a dispatch event for a *main* branch run (e.g., push-emulated dispatch), merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) == HEAD → diff empty → exzone/locksmoke outputs not set → the legs skip.           # resolve fails SAFE: both arms run unconditioned —
          # over-triggering a rare-path leg costs minutes, under-triggering
          # one hides a nightly-only red (the #1309 class).

# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

          - target: android
            runner: ubuntu-latest

          - target: web
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build web --release
          - target: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build linux --release
          - target: windows

    steps:

      - name: ${{ matrix.cmd }}
        working-directory: flutter_app
        shell: bash
        run: ${{ matrix.cmd }}

  # Files ONE deduped issue when the scheduled nightly run goes red: the
  # open `nightly-red` issue is searched first and only commented on, so a
  # persistent failure never spams duplicates. A GREEN scheduled run closes
  # the open issue (the nightly-red tracker is only as good as its sunset).
  #
  # Resurrection (issue #1267 N3): five consecutive red nights
  # (2026-10-01 → 10-05) filed NOTHING. Two defects, both fixed here —
  #  1. the dedup lookup read jq's literal "null" (an empty result of
  #     `.[0].number`) as a truthy issue number, so the no-open-tracker
  #     path died commenting issue "null" and never filed — every lookup
  #     now reads `.[0].number // empty` (both steps);
  #  2. the job was schedule-only, so the AC3 synthetic-red drill could
  #     not reach it — dispatch + fileTracker=true arms it too.
  # The decision (filed / commented / closed / why-not) lands in the job
  # output AND the step summary; two consecutive red scheduled nights add
  # the nightly-red-escalated label (streak counted from the completed
  # schedule-event runs preceding this one — dispatch runs never count).
  auto-issue:
    name: File nightly-red issue
    needs: [full-quality, pty-integration, cli-visual, flutter-app-macos, build-release]
    if: >-
      always() && !cancelled() &&
      (github.event_name == 'schedule' ||
       (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.fileTracker == 'true'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      # issues: write — file/comment/close/label the deduped nightly-red
      # issue. actions: read — the filing leg lists this run's jobs via
      # `gh api repos/.../actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs` and the escalation
      # streak via `gh run list`; a job-level permissions block drops
      # every unlisted scope to none, so without this the calls 403
      # ("Resource not accessible by integration") and no issue is filed.
      issues: write
      actions: read
    steps:
      # AC3 decision-log visibility: the arm/disarm reason is in the job
      # output on EVERY run, red or green, filing or not.
      - name: Filer decision (why-not visibility, #1267 AC3)
        if: always()
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "schedule" ]; then
            echo "filer armed: scheduled run — files/comments/closes the tracker"
          elif [ "${{ github.event.inputs.fileTracker }}" = "true" ]; then
            echo "filer armed: dispatch with fileTracker=true (AC3 synthetic-red drill)"
          else
            echo "filer decision: why-not — manual dispatch without fileTracker=true; pass it to exercise the tracker (AC3 drill)"
          fi

      - name: Close the nightly-red issue on a green run
        # Schedule-only: a manual (drill) dispatch is not a night — its
        # green must never close the live nightly tracker.
        if: success() && github.event_name == 'schedule'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          # `// empty` (issue #1267 N3): an empty result must read EMPTY —
          # jq's bare `.[0].number` prints the literal string "null",
          # which `[ -n ]` treats as a live issue number, so the close
          # died commenting issue "null" (the silent-death bug).
          existing=$(gh issue list --state open --label nightly-red \
            --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty' --repo "$repo")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
              --body "Green again: ${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID} — closing."
            gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo"
            echo "decision: closed #$existing — nightly green again"
            echo "decision: closed #$existing — nightly green again" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "decision: why-not close — no open nightly-red tracker"
            echo "decision: why-not close — no open nightly-red tracker" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      - name: Create or update the nightly-red issue
        if: failure()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          date=$(date -u +%F)
          title="Nightly full-matrix red: ${date}"
          repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          gh label create nightly-red --force \
            --description "Nightly full-quality run is failing" \
            --color B60205 --repo "$repo"
          gh label create nightly-red-escalated --force \
            --description "Nightly red 2+ consecutive scheduled nights (issue #1267 N3)" \
            --color D93F0B --repo "$repo"
          # Failing job names of this run, plus the run URL.
          failing=$(gh api \
            "repos/$repo/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          [ -z "$failing" ] && failing="(unknown)"
          # N3 escalation: consecutive red SCHEDULED nights completed
          # BEFORE this run (this run's own red is the +1). The streak
          # stops at the first non-failure. Dispatch runs never count —
          # the label tracks real nights.
          streak=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow nightly.yml \
            --event schedule --status completed --limit 10 \
            --json conclusion,databaseId \
            --jq 'reduce .[] as $r ({s: 0, done: false};
                  if ($r.databaseId | tostring) == "'"$GITHUB_RUN_ID"'" or .done then .
                  elif $r.conclusion == "failure" then {s: (.s + 1), done: false}
                  else {s: .s, done: true} end) | .s')
          nights=$((streak + 1))
          echo "decision: red night ${nights} in a row (streak input: ${streak} completed failures)"
          body=$(printf 'Nightly full-matrix run is red.\n\nFailing jobs: %s\nRun: %s\nConsecutive red scheduled nights (incl. this one): %s\n' \
            "$failing" "${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" "$nights")
          # Dedup: comment on the existing open nightly-red issue instead of
          # opening a duplicate. --repo everywhere: this job has no checkout,
          # bare `gh` invokes git for repo detection and dies with
          # "not a git repository" (the 2026-09-18 filing-leg failure).
          # `// empty` on the lookup — the literal-"null" bug above.
          existing=$(gh issue list --state open --label nightly-red \
            --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty' --repo "$repo")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --body "$body" --repo "$repo"
            echo "decision: commented the open tracker #$existing (no duplicate filed)"
            echo "decision: commented the open tracker #$existing (no duplicate filed)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            target="$existing"
          else
            target=$(gh issue create --title "$title" --label nightly-red \
              --body "$body" --assignee ai-teammate --repo "$repo")
            echo "decision: filed $target"
            echo "decision: filed $target" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
          if [ "$streak" -ge 1 ]; then
            gh issue edit "$target" --add-label nightly-red-escalated --repo "$repo"
            echo "decision: escalated $target — $nights consecutive red scheduled nights"
            echo "decision: escalated $target — $nights consecutive red scheduled nights" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

Now I have the full picture of the filer. Let me analyze deeper:

**Filer job analysis:**

1. Job `if`: `always() && !cancelled() && (schedule || (workflow_dispatch && fileTracker == 'true'))`. 

2. Close step: `if: success() && github.event_name == 'schedule'` — good.

3. Create/update step: `if: failure()` — runs when any needed job failed. On a RED drill dispatch with fileTracker=true: `failure()` true → files/comments. 

   **Wait — important**: on a red SCHEDULED night, the streak jq runs. On a red DRILL dispatch, the streak jq also runs and counts prior scheduled failures. `--event schedule` filters to scheduled runs only; the current dispatch run is not in the list, but the databaseId exclusion makes it robust anyway.

   **Issue A — escalation on drill dispatches**: If a drill is run right after a real red night (streak >= 1), the drill's synthetic red gets counted as "night N+1" and the tracker is escalated. The body text "Consecutive red scheduled nights (incl. this one): 2" is wrong on a drill (this one is not a scheduled night). Minor/false-positive escalation — SUGGESTION-level. Actually the job comment says "dispatch runs never count" — meaning prior dispatch runs are excluded from the streak, but the CURRENT drill run still adds +1 via nights=streak+1 and can trigger escalation when streak>=1. Contradiction between comment ("dispatch runs never count — the label tracks real nights") and behavior (a drill counts as the triggering night). SUGGESTION.

4. **`nights=$((streak + 1))` with empty streak**: If `gh run list` fails, with `set -e`? Does this step have `set -e`? The step doesn't declare `shell: bash` with set -e. Default shell for run steps on linux is `bash -e {0}` — GitHub's default is `bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail {0}`? Actually the default is `bash -e {0}` (without pipefail). So `set -e` behavior: if `gh run list` fails → `streak=$(...)` assignment fails → step aborts immediately. **The filer would then never file** — the exact silent-death class this PR fixes. However: streak query happens BEFORE the dedup/filing. Order: labels → failing jobs → streak → nights → body → dedup lookup → file/comment → escalate. A transient `gh run list` failure kills filing. But note `gh api` for failing jobs is also before. This risk existed pre-PR with the `gh api` call. The PR adds a NEW network call (gh run list) earlier in the chain — slightly increasing the failure surface of the filing leg. Also if `gh run list` succeeds but outputs empty (no scheduled runs ever — impossible in practice), `streak=""` → `nights=$(( + 1))` = 1, `[ "" -ge 1 ]` → bash test error (integer expression expected), exit code 2 → step fails AFTER filing. With -e, the `[` failure at the END would mark the step red even though filing succeeded. Minor robustness.

   Hmm — actually wait: does `-e` abort on `[ "" -ge 1 ]` returning 2? `[` is a command; if it fails (exit 2) inside an `if` condition, -e does NOT abort (conditions are exempt). `if [ "$streak" -ge 1 ]; then` — the `[` failure inside if-condition just evaluates false → skip escalation. OK so that path is fine.

   The `streak=$(gh run list ...)` failure with -e DOES abort. SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? The streak is needed for the body text ("Consecutive red scheduled nights") — the body is built after. Filing depends on it. A failure here = another silent night. I'd flag as SUGGESTION (low probability, but the whole PR is about making the filer resilient). Maybe IMPORTANT — it partially recreates the bug class the PR exists to fix. Let me think… The PR's core lesson: "the filer died silently for 5 nights; decision logs now make death visible". If streak query fails → step aborts → no filing, BUT the job would be RED (step failure visible in the run + the failed step is visible). The silent-death aspect is fixed by the job going visibly red (previously the job went green while commenting issue "null" — actually did it? The old code died in the middle and the step would fail red too... the old failure mode: `existing="null"` → `gh issue comment "null"` → fails → step red. So it wasn't fully silent — the run was red but no tracker. Hmm, the PR says "five silent red nights filed NOTHING". The step was presumably red but nobody looked; the new decision log + escalation addresses visibility). A streak failure → red step + no filing = same class as before, but now the step logs... nothing (dies before decisions). I'll flag as IMPORTANT with a `|| true` / fallback suggestion: `streak=$(gh run list ... || echo 0)`. Actually more precisely, fail-safe direction for the filer = file WITHOUT streak info. Suggest `streak=$(gh run list ... || echo 0)`.

5. **`gh run list --workflow nightly.yml`** — the file must be referenced as `nightly.yml`. OK.

6. **jq injection via GITHUB_RUN_ID**: `'"$GITHUB_RUN_ID"'` — env var set by GitHub runner, always numeric. Safe.

7. **`title="Nightly full-matrix red: ${date}"`** — dedup by label only, not title. Multiple red nights comment on the same issue. OK.

8. **Dedup race**: none relevant.

9. **The `if: failure()` step and job-level `always()`**: job runs on schedule or drill dispatch. On a GREEN drill: close step skipped (schedule-only), create step skipped (failure() false). 10. **`gh issue edit "$target" --add-label`** — if the label already exists on the issue, gh API add-labels is idempotent. OK.

14. **The `fileTracker` input on workflow_dispatch** — `github.event.inputs.fileTracker == 'true'` works for boolean inputs (stringified). Also could use `inputs.fileTracker`. Fine.

if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            case "$name" in
              build-web|build-android|build-ios|build-macos|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
                  platform_red=true
                fi
                ;;
              *)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ] && [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
                  dart_blocker="a leg is $r ($name)"
                fi
                ;;
            esac
          done
          if [ -n "$dart_blocker" ]; then dart_ok=false; else dart_ok=true; fi
          echo "dart_ok=$dart_ok" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Aggregate verdicts AFTER the export — branch protection is
          # unchanged: ANY red leg (package or platform) still fails this
          # required check; only the PUBLISH gate ignores platform reds.
          [ -z "$dart_blocker" ] || fail "$dart_blocker"
          [ "$platform_red" = "false" ] || fail "a platform/native leg is red — the aggregate is red; dart_ok stays true (publish is not gated on platform legs, #1368), see the leg results above"
          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.

The factory-sm is a reusable workflow from an external repo. The dispatch ref for ci.yml = the PR head SHA presumably. Yes, checkout fetch-depth 0 fetches all refs including origin/main. merge-base works.

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below

On a dispatched run, this checks out the dispatched ref. Good.

**Timing consideration**: If the SM validation dispatch happens when the PR branch is BEHIND main (no recent merge-from-main), merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) = fork point — the diff includes everything the PR changed relative to the fork point. If main moved ahead and the PR touches files that main also changed, the PR's merged differs. Over/under-triggering is bounded. Fine — documented.

**Now a deeper check on the `exit 0` early-return interaction with `set -e`**: GitHub default shell is `bash -e {0}`. In the fail-safe branch:
```bash
BASE_REF="$(git merge-base origin/main "$HEAD_REF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
```
The `|| true` protects against -e. ✓

`if [ -z "$HEAD_REF" ]` — on PR events HEAD_REF non-empty. ✓

`git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" | grep -qE '...'` — inside an `if` condition, so -e doesn't abort on grep non-match. ✓ But `git diff` failing (bad SHAs) inside if-condition → also just evaluates false → outputs unset → legs SKIP (fail-open) on PR events. On dispatch events, HEAD_REF was validated to exist (git rev-parse HEAD) and BASE_REF via merge-base success → diff works. OK.

**What about `pipefail`?** GitHub default doesn't include pipefail. `git diff | grep -q` — grep -q exits early (SIGPIPE for git). Without pipefail, the pipeline status = grep's status. Fine.

**Now, the locksmoke skip-on-main-dispatch regression**: Before this PR, exzone ran on EVERY ci.yml workflow_dispatch — including main validation dispatches and releaseDryRun/releaseDispatch. Now on main dispatches it skips. The PR says the nightly stays the backstop for main. Given #1265/#1266 were nightly-caught, and the whole point is PR gating — fine. But wait, one subtle thing: **releaseDispatch runs the release pipeline** — the release path builds the app itself elsewhere (build-macos.yml etc.)? The release flow has its own legs (installer-verify, fa-aot-build are ci.yml jobs!). Hmm — releaseDryRun/releaseDispatch run INSIDE ci.yml, and its quality-gate aggregates. On a release dispatch on main, exzone/locksmoke now SKIP — quality-gate treats skipped as OK. Before, exzone ran on release dispatches. So the release dispatch LOSES the exzone coverage it had in slice 1. Is that a problem? Exzone = macOS JS-engine tests of flutter_app. The release pipeline itself builds and attaches binaries (installer-verify etc.) but does it RUN the flutter_app test/apps suite? The nightly runs flutter-app-macos (full suite) nightly. Release = from main, which passed the nightly. Hmm, main's last nightly might predate the release commits. It's a small coverage regression on main dispatches, explicitly documented as intended ("Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the nightly flutter-app-macos leg stays the full-suite backstop there"). The ticket's owner directives presumably accept this. OK — documented intent, not a finding. Well — maybe worth a suggestion note: releaseDryRun/releaseDispatch dispatches now skip lock-smoke/exzone; if a release-time lockfile refresh lands directly on main via the release bump (chore/release-vX bump pushes → those are push events on main → exzone skipped on push anyway — never ran on push). Consistent.

**A REAL issue candidate — the `flutter-app-lock-smoke` leg does not run on `push`/`schedule` for main**: lockfile floats arrive via `flutter pub get` DURING resolve (transitive float) — on main pushes, no lock-smoke. The nightly build-release covers main nightly. Documented. Fine.

**Now — the nightly filer job-level `if` with `always()`**: `needs: [full-quality, pty-integration, cli-visual, flutter-app-macos, build-release]` — with `always() && !cancelled()`. On a drill dispatch where a needed job is SKIPPED (e.g., someone dispatches nightly.yml on a branch where some legs are conditional?), skipped needs → failure() false → close/create steps skip → only the decision step logs. Fine.

**Escalation on drill + real red night before — check again**: on a RED drill dispatch (fileTracker=true), `failure()` true → filing step runs. streak counts prior SCHEDULED completed failures. If >= 1 → escalate the drill-filed/commented tracker. The job comment says "dispatch runs never count — the label tracks real nights", but the current drill run DOES count as a red "night" (nights=streak+1). The label description: "Nightly red 2+ consecutive scheduled nights". A drill-triggered escalation labels the tracker as if 2+ real red nights happened when possibly only 1 real red night + 1 drill. → The escalation is meant to page a human for repeated REAL failures; a synthetic drill inflating it is a false-positive page. BUT: drills are rare, deliberate, human-initiated (with fileTracker=true) — the human running the drill knows. And the body text includes the run URL so the responder sees it's a dispatch. I'll rate SUGGESTION: exclude drill dispatches from escalation (only escalate when `github.event_name == 'schedule'`), e.g. `if [ "$streak" -ge 1 ] && [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "schedule" ]`.

Hmm — actually wait. Let me re-read: "two consecutive red SCHEDULED nights add `nightly-red-escalated` (streak = completed schedule-event failures before this run, current run excluded, dispatch runs never count; green resets naturally)". "dispatch runs never count" — the PR's own description says dispatch runs never count! But the implementation: a drill dispatch DOES add the label when streak >= 1 (the drill itself is counted as the +1). So the implementation CONTRADICTS the PR description on this fine point. The streak (prior nights) counts only schedule runs, ✓, but the "+1" includes drill runs. Per the PR text "dispatch runs never count", a drill should not trigger escalation. This is an implementation-vs-description inconsistency — a genuine finding. Severity: it's an edge case (drill right after a real red night, both red) — SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT? The drill is explicitly designed to run on a branch with a forced-failing leg — i.e., ALWAYS red. If an operator runs the drill while the live tracker is open from a real red night, the drill comments on the LIVE tracker (dedup by label) with a "synthetic" red comment and potentially escalates it. Commenting on the live tracker during a drill is by design (AC3: "tracker filed/commented within the same run"). The escalation false-positive: minor but real. I'd say SUGGESTION.

# Nightly full-matrix quality run (issue #177, Wave 3 / AC6): the PR-level

blocks.text:
# Nightly full-matrix quality run (issue #177, Wave 3 / AC6): the PR-level
# ci.yml was slimmed down for speed, so this workflow preserves the original
# monolith semantics — every gate, full thresholds — on a nightly schedule.
# When a scheduled run goes red, the auto-issue job files (or updates) a
# single deduped `nightly-red` issue.
name: Nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      # Issue #1267 AC3: the synthetic-red drill — dispatch the nightly
      # with a forced-failing leg and fileTracker=true; the filer must
      # file or comment the nightly-red tracker WITHIN that same run.
      # Manual dispatches without the flag stay tracker-silent (ad-hoc
      # red runs never spam the tracker; scheduled nights always file).
      fileTracker:
        description: 'File/comment the nightly-red tracker when this run is red (#1267 AC3 drill flag)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — the nightly-red filing job grants
# issues: write (+ actions: read) in its own job-level block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  full-quality:
    name: Full quality gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - run: dart pub get

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings

      # The example Flutter app lives in this repo; without its package
      # config the repo-wide `dart analyze` cannot resolve Flutter imports.
      - name: Example app pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The repo-wide `dart analyze` also walks office_addin/dart; without
      # its package config the analyzer cannot resolve
      # `package:fa_office_agent/...` imports (nightly full-quality was red
      # on email_quarantine_test.dart since the add-in landed). ci.yml's
      # analyze job already does this — nightly must match.
      - name: Office add-in pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        run: dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

machine-merge.yml and sm-kicker.yml both dispatch ci.yml via factory-sm (ci_workflow: ci.yml). Those dispatches happen on PR head SHAs for validation — merge-base works.

Also, check AGENTS.md for review-relevant conventions on CI changes. Let me grep for relevant sections quickly.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a failed streak query kills the filing leg — re-creates the silent-death class this PR fixes**

`nightly.yml:603` runs `streak=$(gh run list ...)` **before** the dedup lookup and the file/comment block. GitHub's default step shell is `bash -e`, so if this call fails transiently (rate limit, 5xx, network blip), the assignment aborts the step **before any issue is filed or commented** — a red night with no tracker, exactly the 5-red-nights failure mode (#1267 N3) this PR resurrects the filer from. The decision log would be empty, which makes it diagnosable, but the filer still dies on metadata.

The escalation streak is informational — filing must not depend on it. Make the streak best-effort:

```bash
streak=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow nightly.yml \
  --event schedule --status completed --limit 10 \
  --json conclusion,databaseId \
  --jq '...' ) || streak=0
```

(or move the streak computation below the file/comment block so it can only affect the escalation, never the filing). Consistent with the PR's own fail-safe principle: a classification failure runs the leg — a streak failure should still file.

💡 **SUGGESTION: a red drill dispatch can add `nightly-red-escalated` after only ONE real red night**

`nightly.yml:610` computes `nights=$((streak + 1))` and `nightly.yml:632` escalates on `[ "$streak" -ge 1 ]` for **any** armed run — including a `fileTracker=true` drill dispatch. The PR description states "dispatch runs never count", but a drill that runs after a single real red night counts its synthetic red as night #2 and labels the tracker `nightly-red-escalated`, whose description reads "Nightly red 2+ consecutive **scheduled** nights" — factually wrong for the drill case (the streak input counts real nights, the +1 does not).

The streak input is already correctly schedule-scoped; gate the +1/escalation the same way:

```bash
if [ "$streak" -ge 1 ] && [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "schedule" ]; then
```

Low impact (drills are rare, deliberate, and the body names the run URL), but it keeps the escalation signal — a human page — reserved for consecutive real red nights.

## PR Description

Fixes #1267 (slice 2 of the epic: N1/AC1 + N2/AC2 + N3/AC3; N4/AC5 remains, see Delivered vs remaining).

Motivating incidents, both CLOSED: #1265 (native build break arrived via an uncommitted lockfile — no PR surface at all) and #1266 (macOS app-suite regression whose only surface was nightly-only). AC4 linkage: both closed before this slice.

## Delivered

**N1/AC1 — path-triggered exclusion-zone leg under dispatch-only CI.** Slice 1 (#1350) landed `flutter-app-exzone` path-BLIND: it ran on EVERY SM validation dispatch because the `changes` classifier had no pull_request event to diff. This slice makes the classifier derive the validated diff itself: on `workflow_dispatch` it computes `merge-base(origin/main, HEAD)` (the PR fork point; the changes checkout is already fetch-depth: 0). A lib/src-only PR no longer pays for the macOS JS-engine leg; a `flutter_app/lib/apps/**` / `lib/src/js_ext/**` / exclusion-test diff does. Classification failure fails SAFE — the rare-path arms run unconditioned (over-triggering costs minutes; under-triggering hides a nightly-only red, the gh-1307/#1309 class). The four group outputs stay with the non-PR filter step, so main dispatches keep the full gate.

**N2/AC2 — lockfile-modified release smoke.** Lockfile committed + `--enforce-lockfile` everywhere already landed (gh-1296/gh-1265). Missing piece: the native linux/windows desktop targets were nightly-only, so a lockfile float (#1265's transitive `flutter_inappwebview`) had no pre-merge surface. New `flutter-app-lock-smoke` matrix (ubuntu + windows) runs `flutter build linux|windows --release` ONLY when the diff modifies `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` — same path-triggered model as exzone, same pinned SDK (`3.47.x`) and Linux toolchain as the nightly build-release legs. The resolve rides the shared `--enforce-lockfile` composite action (#726 retry + skew fail-fast), so a pubspec/lockfile skew fails loudly before any build. A red smoke reddens the required `Quality gate` (platform class per #1368: blocks the merge, never the pure-Dart publish). PRs not touching the lockfile pay nothing.

**N3/AC3 — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation.** Root cause of five silent red nights (last living tracker #466): the dedup lookup read jq's literal `"null"` (empty result of bare `.[0].number`) as a truthy issue number and died commenting issue `"null"` — never filing. - the job arms on `schedule` AND on a new `fileTracker=true` workflow_dispatch input — the AC3 synthetic-red drill (dispatch a forced-failing nightly with the flag → tracker filed/commented within the same run); manual dispatches without the flag stay tracker-silent;
- close-on-green stays schedule-only (a drill dispatch is not a night and must not close the live tracker);
- the decision — filed / commented / closed / why-not — is logged to the job output AND the step summary on every run (an empty decision log is how the filer stayed dead);
- two consecutive red SCHEDULED nights add `nightly-red-escalated` (streak = completed schedule-event failures before this run, current run excluded, dispatch runs never count; green resets naturally).

Note on #1364: that card is the `flake_watch.py` `--search`-based dedup (unquoted `(#<digits>` title fragment) — a DIFFERENT dedup in DIFFERENT code; untouched here, as scoped. The nightly filer's dedup is label-scoped JSON + jq, immune to the search-quoting class.

**Guards.** `test/ci_1267_path_triggered_legs_test.dart` + `test/nightly_filer_1267_test.dart` pin the wiring (structural lint over the workflow YAML — the repo's static-assert pattern, cf. `ci_binaries_arch_gate_test.dart`); `ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart` AC3 count 12 → 13 for the new leg's action use (documented in place).

## Delivered vs remaining (issue ACs)

- AC1 ✅ (path-triggered on both events; a PR touching the external `packages/js_widget_runtime/` arrives as a `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` pin → exzone runs; lib/src-only → skips)
- AC2 ✅ (lock-smoke on lockfile diff; not touching → skipped)
- AC3 ✅ (filer resurrection + drill flag + decision log + escalation — verified by the drill dispatch once CI runs; remote-only surface)
- AC4 ✅ both incidents closed (linked above)
- AC5 / N4 ❌ remaining: merge-snapshot gating (merge queue / merge-bot synthesized tree) + the nightly-test-leg convergence (nightly keeps build/release legs, drops test legs once the snapshot run absorbs them) + subsuming the #1282 binaries-pr dispatch wiring into the snapshot gate. Owner directives 2026-10-05 recorded in the issue; that slice intentionally left out of this PR — it changes the merge flow itself, not the leg topology.
- N4-convergence caveat respected: nightly test legs are NOT touched here — until the merge-snapshot gate exists, the nightly full matrix stays main's backstop.

## Verification

Local dart is unavailable on this box (flutter shim cannot write its cache) — remote CI verifies. The workflow YAML is ruby-YAML validated, job ids/needs statically resolved, and the two new guard tests are pure text/YAML asserts runnable in the existing test-core shards. The legs themselves (macOS JS-engine run, linux/windows release builds, the filer's gh calls) get no local tests — they are CI-only surfaces, exercised by the first dispatch/nightly runs; the AC3 drill procedure is: `gh workflow run nightly.yml -f fileTracker=true` on a branch with a forced-failing leg, then expect the tracker comment inside that run.

          # resolve fails SAFE: both arms run unconditioned —
          # over-triggering a rare-path leg costs minutes, under-triggering
          # one hides a nightly-only red (the #1309 class).

            HEAD_REF="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (issue #1267 N1 slice 2): ci.yml has NO pull_request
  # trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM workflow_dispatch on the head
  # SHA (machine-sm.yml). The changes classifier derives the validated diff
  # under BOTH events (merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) on dispatches), so
  # this leg is PATH-TRIGGERED: a PR touching only lib/src core never pays
  # for it (AC1), a lib/apps + js_ext diff does, and a classifier failure
  # fails safe (the leg runs). Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it —
  # the nightly flutter-app-macos leg stays the full-suite backstop there.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N2 (AC2) — lockfile-modified release smoke. Resolution
  # floats transitive deps to latest-compatible on every resolve, and the
  # breaking arrival (#1265: a transitive flutter_inappwebview nobody
  # declares) lands as a flutter_app/pubspec.lock diff — a surface the PR
  # legs never built: the native linux/windows desktop targets were
  # nightly-only (nightly.yml build-release), so the break surfaced as the
  # 5-red-nights window instead of a red PR. When the diff MODIFIES the
  # lockfile, this matrix release-builds the app on linux+windows pre-merge
  # (the same two targets the nightly carries); every other PR pays
  # nothing. The resolve rides the shared composite action (--enforce-
  # lockfile, #726 retry, skew fail-fast — test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_
  # test.dart), so a pubspec/lockfile skew fails HERE loudly before any
  # build step. Path-triggered like exzone: pull_request events AND SM
  # validation dispatches (merge-base diff in the classifier, fail-safe).
  # Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the nightly build-release
  # matrix stays the backstop, and a red leg reddens the required Quality
  # gate (platform class — it must block the merge, never the pure-Dart
  # publish, #1368).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-lock-smoke:
    name: Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.locksmoke == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
          - os: windows
            runner: windows-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Same pinned SDK as the nightly build-release legs (#281).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      # Linux desktop toolchain + plugin native deps (gtk3 for the runner,
      # gstreamer for audioplayers_linux) — same as the nightly linux leg.
      - name: Install Linux desktop toolchain
        if: matrix.os == 'linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y clang cmake ninja-build pkg-config \
            libgtk-3-dev liblzma-dev libstdc++-12-dev \
            libgstreamer1.0-dev libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Create placeholder firebase_options.dart
        shell: bash
        run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: flutter build ${{ matrix.os }} --release (lockfile smoke)

        shell: bash

    permissions:

      matrix:
        include:
          - target: macos
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build macos --release
          - target: ios
            runner: macos-latest
            cmd: flutter build ios --release --no-codesign
          - target: android
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build apk --flavor store --release
          - target: web
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build web --release
          - target: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            cmd: flutter build linux --release
          - target: windows
            runner: windows-latest
            cmd: flutter build windows --release
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Same pinned SDK as the PR build legs and the release path (#281).

  # Files ONE deduped issue when the scheduled nightly run goes red: the
  # open `nightly-red` issue is searched first and only commented on, so a
  # persistent failure never spams duplicates. A GREEN scheduled run closes
  # the open issue (the nightly-red tracker is only as good as its sunset).
  #
  # Resurrection (issue #1267 N3): five consecutive red nights
  # (2026-10-01 → 10-05) filed NOTHING. Two defects, both fixed here —
  #  1. the dedup lookup read jq's literal "null" (an empty result of
  #     `.[0].number`) as a truthy issue number, so the no-open-tracker
  #     path died commenting issue "null" and never filed — every lookup
  #     now reads `.[0].number // empty` (both steps);
  #  2. the job was schedule-only, so the AC3 synthetic-red drill could
  #     not reach it — dispatch + fileTracker=true arms it too.
  # The decision (filed / commented / closed / why-not) lands in the job
  # output AND the step summary; two consecutive red scheduled nights add
  # the nightly-red-escalated label (streak counted from the completed
  # schedule-event runs preceding this one — dispatch runs never count).
  auto-issue:
    name: File nightly-red issue
    needs: [full-quality, pty-integration, cli-visual, flutter-app-macos, build-release]
    if: >-
      always() && !cancelled() &&
      (github.event_name == 'schedule' ||
       (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.fileTracker == 'true'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      # issues: write — file/comment/close/label the deduped nightly-red
      # issue. actions: read — the filing leg lists this run's jobs via
      # `gh api repos/.../actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs` and the escalation
      # streak via `gh run list`; a job-level permissions block drops
      # every unlisted scope to none, so without this the calls 403
      # ("Resource not accessible by integration") and no issue is filed.
      issues: write
      actions: read
    steps:
      # AC3 decision-log visibility: the arm/disarm reason is in the job
      # output on EVERY run, red or green, filing or not.
      - name: Filer decision (why-not visibility, #1267 AC3)
        if: always()
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "schedule" ]; then
            echo "filer armed: scheduled run — files/comments/closes the tracker"
          elif [ "${{ github.event.inputs.fileTracker }}" = "true" ]; then
            echo "filer armed: dispatch with fileTracker=true (AC3 synthetic-red drill)"
          else
            echo "filer decision: why-not — manual dispatch without fileTracker=true; pass it to exercise the tracker (AC3 drill)"
          fi

      - name: Close the nightly-red issue on a green run
        # Schedule-only: a manual (drill) dispatch is not a night — its
        # green must never close the live nightly tracker.
        if: success() && github.event_name == 'schedule'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          # `// empty` (issue #1267 N3): an empty result must read EMPTY —
          # jq's bare `.[0].number` prints the literal string "null",
          # which `[ -n ]` treats as a live issue number, so the close
          # died commenting issue "null" (the silent-death bug).
          existing=$(gh issue list --state open --label nightly-red \
            --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty' --repo "$repo")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
              --body "Green again: ${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID} — closing."
            gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo"
            echo "decision: closed #$existing — nightly green again"
            echo "decision: closed #$existing — nightly green again" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "decision: why-not close — no open nightly-red tracker"
            echo "decision: why-not close — no open nightly-red tracker" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      - name: Create or update the nightly-red issue
        if: failure()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          date=$(date -u +%F)
          title="Nightly full-matrix red: ${date}"
          repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          gh label create nightly-red --force \
            --description "Nightly full-quality run is failing" \
            --color B60205 --repo "$repo"
          gh label create nightly-red-escalated --force \
            --description "Nightly red 2+ consecutive scheduled nights (issue #1267 N3)" \
            --color D93F0B --repo "$repo"
          # Failing job names of this run, plus the run URL.
          failing=$(gh api \
            "repos/$repo/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          [ -z "$failing" ] && failing="(unknown)"
          # N3 escalation: consecutive red SCHEDULED nights completed
          # BEFORE this run (this run's own red is the +1). The streak
          # stops at the first non-failure. Dispatch runs never count —
          # the label tracks real nights.
          streak=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow nightly.yml \
            --event schedule --status completed --limit 10 \
            --json conclusion,databaseId \
            --jq 'reduce .[] as $r ({s: 0, done: false};
                  if ($r.databaseId | tostring) == "'"$GITHUB_RUN_ID"'" or .done then .
                  elif $r.conclusion == "failure" then {s: (.s + 1), done: false}
                  else {s: .s, done: true} end) | .s')
          nights=$((streak + 1))
          echo "decision: red night ${nights} in a row (streak input: ${streak} completed failures)"
          body=$(printf 'Nightly full-matrix run is red.\n\nFailing jobs: %s\nRun: %s\nConsecutive red scheduled nights (incl. this one): %s\n' \
            "$failing" "${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${repo}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" "$nights")
          # Dedup: comment on the existing open nightly-red issue instead of
          # opening a duplicate. --repo everywhere: this job has no checkout,
          # bare `gh` invokes git for repo detection and dies with
          # "not a git repository" (the 2026-09-18 filing-leg failure).
          # `// empty` on the lookup — the literal-"null" bug above.
          existing=$(gh issue list --state open --label nightly-red \
            --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty' --repo "$repo")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --body "$body" --repo "$repo"
            echo "decision: commented the open tracker #$existing (no duplicate filed)"
            echo "decision: commented the open tracker #$existing (no duplicate filed)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            target="$existing"
          else
            target=$(gh issue create --title "$title" --label nightly-red \
              --body "$body" --assignee ai-teammate --repo "$repo")
            echo "decision: filed $target"
            echo "decision: filed $target" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
          if [ "$streak" -ge 1 ]; then
            gh issue edit "$target" --add-label nightly-red-escalated --repo "$repo"
            echo "decision: escalated $target — $nights consecutive red scheduled nights"
            echo "decision: escalated $target — $nights consecutive red scheduled nights" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

On a red DRILL dispatch, the streak jq also runs and counts prior scheduled failures. `--event schedule` filters to scheduled runs only; the current dispatch run is not in the list, but the databaseId exclusion makes it robust anyway.

   **Issue A — escalation on drill dispatches**: If a drill is run right after a real red night (streak >= 1), the drill's synthetic red gets counted as "night N+1" and the tracker is escalated. The body text "Consecutive red scheduled nights (incl. this one): 2" is wrong on a drill (this one is not a scheduled night). Minor/false-positive escalation — SUGGESTION-level. Actually the job comment says "dispatch runs never count" — meaning prior dispatch runs are excluded from the streak, but the CURRENT drill run still adds +1 via nights=streak+1 and can trigger escalation when streak>=1. Contradiction between comment ("dispatch runs never count — the label tracks real nights") and behavior (a drill counts as the triggering night). SUGGESTION.

4. **`nights=$((streak + 1))` with empty streak**: If `gh run list` fails, with `set -e`? Does this step have `set -e`? The step doesn't declare `shell: bash` with set -e. Default shell for run steps on linux is `bash -e {0}` — GitHub's default is `bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail {0}`? Actually the default is `bash -e {0}` (without pipefail). So `set -e` behavior: if `gh run list` fails → `streak=$(...)` assignment fails → step aborts immediately. **The filer would then never file** — the exact silent-death class this PR fixes. However: streak query happens BEFORE the dedup/filing. Order: labels → failing jobs → streak → nights → body → dedup lookup → file/comment → escalate. A transient `gh run list` failure kills filing. But note `gh api` for failing jobs is also before. This risk existed pre-PR with the `gh api` call. The PR adds a NEW network call (gh run list) earlier in the chain — slightly increasing the failure surface of the filing leg. Also if `gh run list` succeeds but outputs empty (no scheduled runs ever — impossible in practice), `streak=""` → `nights=$(( + 1))` = 1, `[ "" -ge 1 ]` → bash test error (integer expression expected), exit code 2 → step fails AFTER filing. With -e, the `[` failure at the END would mark the step red even though filing succeeded. Minor robustness.

OK so that path is fine.

if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
            [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          fi
          # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
          #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            case "$name" in
              build-web|build-android|build-ios|build-macos|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
                  platform_red=true
                fi
                ;;
              *)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ] && [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
                  dart_blocker="a leg is $r ($name)"
                fi
                ;;
            esac
          done
          if [ -n "$dart_blocker" ]; then dart_ok=false; else dart_ok=true; fi
          echo "dart_ok=$dart_ok" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Aggregate verdicts AFTER the export — branch protection is
          # unchanged: ANY red leg (package or platform) still fails this
          # required check; only the PUBLISH gate ignores platform reds.
          [ -z "$dart_blocker" ] || fail "$dart_blocker"
          [ "$platform_red" = "false" ] || fail "a platform/native leg is red — the aggregate is red; dart_ok stays true (publish is not gated on platform legs, #1368), see the leg results above"
          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.

# Nightly full-matrix quality run (issue #177, Wave 3 / AC6): the PR-level
# ci.yml was slimmed down for speed, so this workflow preserves the original

blocks.text:
# Nightly full-matrix quality run (issue #177, Wave 3 / AC6): the PR-level
# ci.yml was slimmed down for speed, so this workflow preserves the original
# monolith semantics — every gate, full thresholds — on a nightly schedule.
# When a scheduled run goes red, the auto-issue job files (or updates) a
# single deduped `nightly-red` issue.
name: Nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      # Issue #1267 AC3: the synthetic-red drill — dispatch the nightly
      # with a forced-failing leg and fileTracker=true; the filer must
      # file or comment the nightly-red tracker WITHIN that same run.
      # Manual dispatches without the flag stay tracker-silent (ad-hoc
      # red runs never spam the tracker; scheduled nights always file).
      fileTracker:
        description: 'File/comment the nightly-red tracker when this run is red (#1267 AC3 drill flag)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — the nightly-red filing job grants
# issues: write (+ actions: read) in its own job-level block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  full-quality:
    name: Full quality gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - run: dart pub get

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings

      # The example Flutter app lives in this repo; without its package
      # config the repo-wide `dart analyze` cannot resolve Flutter imports.
      - name: Example app pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The repo-wide `dart analyze` also walks office_addin/dart; without
      # its package config the analyzer cannot resolve
      # `package:fa_office_agent/...` imports (nightly full-quality was red
      # on email_quarantine_test.dart since the add-in landed). ci.yml's
      # analyze job already does this — nightly must match.
      - name: Office add-in pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        run: dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

# pr-1457: ci(1267): path-triggered legs under dispatch-only CI (N1 AC1 + N2 lock-smoke) + nightly-red filer resurrection (N3)

## Description

Fixes #1267 (slice 2 of the epic: N1/AC1 + N2/AC2 + N3/AC3; N4/AC5 remains, see Delivered vs remaining).

Motivating incidents, both CLOSED: #1265 (native build break arrived via an uncommitted lockfile — no PR surface at all) and #1266 (macOS app-suite regression whose only surface was nightly-only). AC4 linkage: both closed before this slice.

## Delivered

**N1/AC1 — path-triggered exclusion-zone leg under dispatch-only CI.** Slice 1 (#1350) landed `flutter-app-exzone` path-BLIND: it ran on EVERY SM validation dispatch because the `changes` classifier had no pull_request event to diff. This slice makes the classifier derive the validated diff itself: on `workflow_dispatch` it computes `merge-base(origin/main, HEAD)` (the PR fork point; the changes checkout is already fetch-depth: 0). A lib/src-only PR no longer pays for the macOS JS-engine leg; a `flutter_app/lib/apps/**` / `lib/src/js_ext/**` / exclusion-test diff does. Classification failure fails SAFE — the rare-path arms run unconditioned (over-triggering costs minutes; under-triggering hides a nightly-only red, the gh-1307/#1309 class). The four group outputs stay with the non-PR filter step, so main dispatches keep the full gate.

**N2/AC2 — lockfile-modified release smoke.** Lockfile committed + `--enforce-lockfile` everywhere already landed (gh-1296/gh-1265). Missing piece: the native linux/windows desktop targets were nightly-only, so a lockfile float (#1265's transitive `flutter_inappwebview`) had no pre-merge surface. New `flutter-app-lock-smoke` matrix (ubuntu + windows) runs `flutter build linux|windows --release` ONLY when the diff modifies `flutter_app/pubspec.lock` — same path-triggered model as exzone, same pinned SDK (`3.47.x`) and Linux toolchain as the nightly build-release legs. The resolve rides the shared `--enforce-lockfile` composite action (#726 retry + skew fail-fast), so a pubspec/lockfile skew fails loudly before any build. A red smoke reddens the required `Quality gate` (platform class per #1368: blocks the merge, never the pure-Dart publish). PRs not touching the lockfile pay nothing.

**N3/AC3 — nightly-red filer resurrection + escalation.** Root cause of five silent red nights (last living tracker #466): the dedup lookup read jq's literal `"null"` (empty result of bare `.[0].number`) as a truthy issue number and died commenting issue `"null"` — never filing. Fixed with `.[0].number // empty` in BOTH steps (the shape ci.yml's ci-red-report already uses). Additionally:
- the job arms on `schedule` AND on a new `fileTracker=true` workflow_dispatch input — the AC3 synthetic-red drill (dispatch a forced-failing nightly with the flag → tracker filed/commented within the same run); manual dispatches without the flag stay tracker-silent;

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N1 — the macOS exclusion-zone leg. By #177 design the ubuntu
  # PR leg never EXERCISES the JS-engine suites: flutter_app/test/apps/**
  # skip their engine-dependent tests on ubuntu (native_test_guard.dart
  # finds no QuickJS .so on a bare runner), so that surface ran only in the
  # nightly macOS leg — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307: an
  # apps/engine regression merged green and went red the same night).
  #
  # Trigger model (issue #1267 N1 slice 2): ci.yml has NO pull_request
  # trigger — PR validation arrives as an SM workflow_dispatch on the head
  # SHA (machine-sm.yml). The changes classifier derives the validated diff
  # under BOTH events (merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) on dispatches), so
  # this leg is PATH-TRIGGERED: a PR touching only lib/src core never pays
  # for it (AC1), a lib/apps + js_ext diff does, and a classifier failure
  # fails safe (the leg runs). Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it —
  # the nightly flutter-app-macos leg stays the full-suite backstop there.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-exzone:
    name: Exclusion zone (macOS JS-engine tests)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      needs.changes.outputs.exzone == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      # Same SDK incantation as the nightly flutter-app-macos leg.
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
      # The guard resolves true on macOS (JavaScriptCore), so the
      # engine-dependent tests RUN here instead of skipping as on ubuntu.
      - name: flutter test test/apps (JS engine live)
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #1267 N2 (AC2) — lockfile-modified release smoke. Resolution
  # floats transitive deps to latest-compatible on every resolve, and the
  # breaking arrival (#1265: a transitive flutter_inappwebview nobody
  # declares) lands as a flutter_app/pubspec.lock diff — a surface the PR
  # legs never built: the native linux/windows desktop targets were
  # nightly-only (nightly.yml build-release), so the break surfaced as the
  # 5-red-nights window instead of a red PR. When the diff MODIFIES the
  # lockfile, this matrix release-builds the app on linux+windows pre-merge
  # (the same two targets the nightly carries); every other PR pays
  # nothing. The resolve rides the shared composite action (--enforce-
  # lockfile, #726 retry, skew fail-fast — test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_
  # test.dart), so a pubspec/lockfile skew fails HERE loudly before any
  # build step. Path-triggered like exzone: pull_request events AND SM
  # validation dispatches (merge-base diff in the classifier, fail-safe).
  # Main/tag/schedule/release runs skip it — the nightly build-release
  # matrix stays the backstop, and a red leg reddens the required Quality
  # gate (platform class — it must block the merge, never the pure-Dart
  # publish, #1368).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  flutter-app-lock-smoke:
    name: Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&

    permissions:

      matrix:

          - os: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
          - os: windows
            runner: windows-latest

      - name: ${{ matrix.cmd }}
